title: Chocolate: Meet a Real Willy Wonka

blanks.sentence: Information for new ideas comes from _____ around the world.
blanks.section: NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS — Developing a new chocolate bar

blanks.sentence: The team creates both the product and its _____.
A product that sells poorly can teach the team useful _____ about its work.
The company starts promoting a new bar when consumer _____ is strong.
Blueberry Truffle and the heart-shaped Geisha bar are examples of products that were commercially _____.

multipleChoice.question: How does the developer's actual work differ from the imagined job of travelling simply to eat chocolate?
options: She collects customer orders from shops before designing each bar.
She judges when new ideas should be developed and brought to market.
She samples finished bars abroad before choosing a factory to produce them.
She visits international stores to copy their most popular chocolate bars.

multipleChoice.question: What chiefly makes the developer feel proud when a new product is well received?
options: Her opportunity to taste more chocolate than other employees.
Her success in finding raw materials at a lower cost.
Her personal decision about when the product should go on sale.
Her team's work in creating the product and its taste experience.

multipleChoice.question: How does the developer compare products that fail with those that sell well?
options: Both can be valuable because an unsuccessful product teaches the team something.
Both deserve the same advertising because sales cannot reveal their quality.
Failed products are more valuable because they are easier to develop again.
Strong-selling products provide more useful feedback than failed ones can.

multipleChoice.question: What order of events is described when demand for a new bar is strong?
options: Shops stock the bar, then the company decides whether to promote it.
Customers choose the bar, then the team begins developing it.
The company promotes the bar before it becomes available in shops.
The company promotes the bar only after customers reject its first version.

multipleChoice.question: What do the examples of Blueberry Truffle and the Geisha bar show about the developer's work?
options: New chocolate bars are generally designed as pairs of products.
She has produced notable hits, although not every new bar succeeds.
Fruit flavours and unusual shapes now guide most of her team's designs.
These bars succeeded chiefly because of the way they were packaged.
